title: The $0 airline settlement that changed airport workers’ health coverage rules

beats.text: A $0 airline settlement changed what airport employers must offer workers.

visual.sub: The settlement specified a change to the law

beats.text: The trade group agreed to dismiss its lawsuit if San Francisco changed the law.

beats.text: It could bring the case back if the Board later increased employers’ obligations.

beats.text: In 2026, one option tied the hourly minimum to family size.

visual.kicker: The rules in 2026 depended on employer choice and family size

beats.text: It ranged from six dollars and seventeen cents to seventeen dollars and forty-four cents.
Employers could still choose a family plan or the City Option.

visual.kicker: The rules in 2026 depended on employer choice and family size

beats.text: The new law sets a single hourly minimum, $2 above the general rate.

visual.kicker: The companion ordinance replaced the family-size formula

beats.text: It also allows an employer to offer a qualifying insurance plan.

visual.kicker: The companion ordinance replaced the family-size formula

beats.text: That plan must cover at least 84 percent of costs on an actuarial basis.
Workers pay no premium for individual coverage. Family premiums have a separate cap.
In 2025, the court kept the case alive. Worker costs still need new records.
